Hi Danielle —

Appreciate the inventory. High level answers to get us started, and I can walk through specifics on the call: 

- Node pools: suggest a three-tier model: (1) control/infra (small m4-style, tainted), (2) inference-GPU (pinned GPUs, isolated NVMe local cache), and (3) ephemeral-workers (preemptible/burst, autoscaled). For A10G-equivalent nodes we recommend 24–32GB RAM per GPU and a minimal host image with our NVMe-friendly kernel patches.
- Storage classes: fast-ssd (local NVMe via local PV + CSI LVM for model cache), encrypted-block (network-attached encrypted volumes for checkpoints), and archive (object-backed volumes). Reclaim policy: Retain for inference model volumes by default; delete for ephemeral scratch. Snapshot strategy: hourly model-cache checkpoints (retained 6h), daily full-volume snapshots for checkpoints (retain 30 days). We support CMK integration for KMS — send KMS ARN and we'll map the flow.
- Network: Calico is fine; recommend policy-inherited namespaces and egress allowed-list by CIDR. Redwood control-plane webhooks can be placed in a management subnet; we prefer an explicit route or VPN tunnel for webhook traffic rather than exposing public endpoints.
- Backup/DR: Velero works to S3-compatible storage; ensure object path perms for profile-level backups.

I've attached a short reference with our on-prem defaults and the preflight checklist. If tomorrow 10:00–10:45 PT works, I'll invite Marissa and Irene from delivery to join.

Sean — quick notes below, will expand into the CSV tonight.

- GPU profile: A10G-equivalent -> 1 GPU node: 1xA10G, 32GB host RAM, 2x1TB NVMe (RAID0 for cache; application-level replication required). For multi-GPU pods, prefer 2xA10G with 64GB host RAM and PCIe topology-aware placement. Host patches: latest kernel LTS with NVMe IO schedulers set to none, driver 5.x+ for best perf.
- Image: minimal distro (Ubuntu 22.04 minimal) + our kernel tuning script, containerd, and our KV cache agent installed.
- CSI choices: local-lvm for model cache (fast-ssd, ephemeral), csi-rbd (or iscsi) for encrypted-block; use snapshotClass tied to backend snapshotter. Reclaim: Retain for model volumes, Delete for ephemeral scratch.
- Snapshots: model-cache hourly (6-hour rolling window), checkpoint volumes daily (retain 30d), backups to object store nightly. We'll provide the velero hooks and plugin list.
- Netpols: namespace-scoped allow-lists; egress controlled via gateway nodes per-rack. For webhooks: ask customer to provide a CIDR or a static NAT egress IP. If they cannot provide static IPs, we fall back to mutual TLS and a client cert exchange.

I'll push the CSV and netpol template to the shared drive in 90 minutes.
